item.title: using Lua scripts
item.description:
#overview

darktable can execute scripts written in Lua to perform an extensive array of actions. Some examples include calling external applications (e.g. after exporting an image), creating keyboard shortcuts that trigger multiple actions in one keystroke, or building entire utility modules.

darktable comes with a number of scripts included. The central orchestrator for scripts is the utility module scripts available in the lighttable. Before darktable 5.6 scripts had to be installed first.

item.title: writing Lua scripts
item.description:
Lua scripts can be used to define actions for darktable to perform when an event is triggered.

Lua is an independent project providing a powerful, fast, lightweight, embeddable scripting language. darktable uses Lua version 5.4. Describing the principles and syntax of Lua is beyond the scope of this manual, so for details see the Lua Reference manual.

One example where a new Lua script might be useful would be calling an external application during file export in order to apply additional processing steps outside of darktable.
